title: bug: live-goal-release.test.tsx reds the whole control-room lane under suite load but passes 3/3 alone
description:
Filed by worker-bcaa6d5e from parent task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5 (Gate 3 roll-up, step 3 gate run, 2026-09-08T20:0xZ). NOT a defect of that parent — its diff is empty — and NOT a defect of any of its three children; measured to task-3697c02bf2ab41a896fcfacb125d9e46.

REPRO. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` at HEAD 8b785725:
  Test Files  1 failed | 204 passed (205)
       Tests  1 failed | 2676 passed (2677)
  FAIL src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx > the refusal path is unchanged by the fix > keeps a transport abort and a daemon refusal at different codes AND different layers
  TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="cr.release.answer"]
Reproduced 2/2 full-suite runs (23:01:05 and 23:01:53 local). The SAME file run alone passes 3/3: `cd apps/control-room && npx vitest run src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx` => `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 4 passed (4)`, three consecutive times.

DIAGNOSIS FROM THE DUMP, not inferred. The rendered DOM in the failure is the card MID-SUBMIT: the button reads `Recording your decision...` and is `disabled`, and `cr.release.base` is `disabled` — i.e. `busy === true`. `cr.release.answer` only renders once `answer !== null`, so the helper at live-goal-release.test.tsx:211 `screen.getByTestId("cr.release.answer").querySelector("code")` is a SYNCHRONOUS read taken before the submit promise has settled. Called from :284. Under an otherwise-idle machine the microtask drains before the assertion; under full-suite load it does not. Same class as gotcha-a-5s-default-timeout-flake-is-contention-not-work. Likely fix: `await screen.findByTestId("cr.release.answer")` (or wrap the click in `await act`) instead of the sync `getByTestId` — a test-only change; no evidence the production card is wrong.

OWNERSHIP MEASURED. `git log -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx` returns exactly ONE commit, 2569dd4e (task-3697c02b, "bug: a live release.decide outruns the browser's 15s transport abort"), authored 2026-09-08 21:40:21 +0300 = 18:40:21Z. The file is CLEAN at HEAD (`git status --porcelain` on it is empty), so this is landed bytes, not peer dirt. That commit is 35 minutes AFTER task-817d893f's completion 00c88cd8 (18:05:17Z, control-room `Test Files 204 passed (204)` / `Tests 2673 passed (2673)` EXIT 0), which is why the Gate 3 children's own green gates never saw it.

WHY IT ESCAPED ITS OWN ROW'S GATE: task-3697c02b's recorded verification is `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room exec vitest run --exclude src/live/live-runs.test.ts` => 204 files / 2621 tests EXIT 0. That run EXCLUDES a file and lands 204/2621 against the full lane's 205/2677, so it is not the lane gate its DoD stands on. Worth pinning in the fix: the gate for a control-room row is the unexcluded `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.

DoD SUGGESTION: make the assertion await the answer, then prove non-vacuity — the arm must still go RED when the production `answer` state is mutated to swallow the refusal code/layer distinction (rail 1: assert the code AND which layer refused, not merely that it refused), and quote an unexcluded `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` count line at 205 files.
definitionOfDone: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (NO --exclude) is EXIT 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim at 205 files / 2677+ tests, run twice consecutively so a load-dependent flake cannot pass once by luck.

The repaired arm is proven non-vacuous by mutation: make the production `live-goal-release.tsx` answer path collapse the transport-abort code/layer into the daemon-refusal code/layer and confirm the arm goes RED, then restore and prove the restore by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup keyed on BOTH the task id and the worker id, in a call separate from the restore.

No production behaviour change is made unless a defect in `live-goal-release.tsx` is actually measured; if the fix is test-only, say so explicitly in the completion record rather than editing the component to make a test pass.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE MECHANISM AND FIND BOTH UNGUARDED READS. NO EDITS.

Read the chain and satisfy yourself the defect is structural, not probabilistic:
- goal-release.tsx:92-103 `decide()` is FIRE-AND-FORGET: `void port.submit(...).then((outcome) => { setAnswer(outcome); setBusy(false); }, ...)`. The click handler returns at once.
- live-goal-release.test.tsx:135-139 `confirmRelease()` ends with `await act(async () => { fireEvent.click(...) })`, which has no contract to await that DETACHED chain. The chain is several ticks deep — the port wrapper at live-goal-release.tsx:70-86, then `transport.sendCommand` at the test's :122 (an async fn returning another promise), plus the `refresh()` that fires the stubbed fetch.
- So the synchronous read at :211 is unguarded BY CONSTRUCTION. The DOM in the filing — button reading `Recording your decision...`, `cr.release.base` disabled — is exactly `busy === true` with `answer === null`.

NOW COUNT THE CALL SITES, because the filing names only one. `answerCode()` is called at :232, :239, :284 and :295. `:239` and `:295` each follow a `settle()` and are already covered. `:284` is the one that reds. `:232` IS THE IDENTICAL UNGUARDED SHAPE — `await confirmRelease()` at :229 then a synchronous read at :232, with only a sync `expect(wire.sends())` between them, which drains nothing. Confirm that yourself by reading; a repair aimed at :284 alone leaves an equally flaky arm eight lines above it.

REPRODUCE UNDER CONTENTION, and note this row is the opposite of every other gate on this board: it WANTS load. The arm passes 3/3 alone — measured at plan time, `cd apps/control-room && npx vitest run src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` gives `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 4 passed (4)` with the four arms at 45/10/6/13ms. So a green single-file run tells you nothing. Run the full lane, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, and if a peer is running a suite at the same time that is the ideal window, not a reason to wait. full-suite-gate was HELD by worker-409b958a at plan time (acquired 10:00:13Z, 15-minute eta). If you cannot reproduce it, say so plainly and proceed on the structural argument — do not manufacture a repro.

Both files are CLEAN landed bytes at HEAD: `git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/` was empty at plan time. Re-check before editing.

PROVE THE REPAIRED ARM IS NON-VACUOUS (DoD 2).

A drain that makes an assertion wait is one refactor away from a drain that makes it never look. Mutate the production surface and confirm the arm goes RED.

THE MUTATION, in the file DoD 2 names: `live-goal-release.tsx`. The port wrapper at :67-88 is where the submit result passes through on its way to `setAnswer`, and :76 (`result.ok || result.layer !== CONTROL_ROOM_TRANSPORT_LAYER`) is the seam that knows the two paths apart. Rewrite the returned result there so a transport abort carries the daemon refusal's code and layer — that is precisely the collapse DoD 2 asks for. Confirm the arm at :279 goes RED on the ASSERTION at :299-300 (`aborted` no longer differs from `refused`), NOT on a timeout: an assertion red proves the arm still reads a real answer; a timeout red would mean the drain is hiding the failure.

WHILE YOU ARE THERE, drill the fix itself: revert `answerCode` to the synchronous form and confirm the repaired arms can still be made to fail. If they stay green under contention with the sync read restored, you have not reproduced the defect and the repair is unproven — say so rather than claiming it.

RESTORE PROOF, and `git diff` alone is not it. `live-goal-release.tsx` is TRACKED and CLEAN, and the checkout is shared. Before mutating: `git status --porcelain` the exact path, copy it out of tree to `%TEMP%` under a name carrying BOTH this task id and your worker id, and record the SHA256 taken FROM THE LIVE FILE at that moment. Restore by copying the backup back. Prove it by SHA256 equality against that pre-mutation hash, in a call SEPARATE from the restore — a copy can silently no-op and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved. A backup keyed only on a seat id can hold a stale vintage from an earlier session, which is why the task id is in the path.

THE LANE GATE, TWICE, UNEXCLUDED (DoD 1).

Run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — NO `--exclude` — twice consecutively, and quote the exit code and the `Test Files N passed` count line VERBATIM for each run. The unexcluded lane is the point of the clause: the row that landed this file recorded `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room exec vitest run --exclude src/live/live-runs.test.ts` at 204 files / 2621 tests, which is not the lane its DoD stood on, and that is exactly how this defect reached the board.

THE COUNT IN DoD 1 IS A REFERENCE, NOT A LITERAL TO MATCH. It says "205 files / 2677+ tests", but epic rail 3 forbids freezing a roster count precisely because concurrent rows move these numbers. Take the PRINTED count as authoritative: a HIGHER count satisfies the clause and should be reported as such with a one-line note that a sibling row added tests. Only a LOWER file count, or any nonzero failed count, is a failure. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code — a run that matched no files prints "No test files found" and exits 0.

Run at least one of the two under real contention if you can arrange it. Two green runs on a quiet host are consistent with the flake still being present; what makes them meaningful is that the drain is deterministic, so say which runs were loaded and which were quiet.

This is one package's lane and it does not need the root suite. `pnpm test` would not cover it anyway — the root vitest include has no `apps/**` — so do not quote a root count as evidence for this clause. If you also run other legs, label them; this DoD is about the control-room lane.

SAY WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY WAS, THEN THE ADVERSARIAL PASS (DoD 3).

DoD 3 is a record obligation and it is the one a rushed close gets wrong. State explicitly in the completion record that the fix is TEST-ONLY, that no defect was measured in `live-goal-release.tsx`, and that the component was touched only by the step 3 mutation drill and restored with the SHA256 proof quoted. If you DID measure a production defect, say what you measured and name it — but do not edit the component to make a test pass, which is what the clause exists to prevent.

Name both repaired call sites in the record, not just the one the filing reported. `:232` was the same unguarded shape as `:284` and a record that mentions only `:284` understates what shipped.

Put the run-by-run count lines in a row COMMENT rather than the completion summary: the summary truncates silently at 2000 characters and a severed gate table reads as a skipped gate.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: does any other arm in this file read state synchronously after an action that dispatches a detached promise — check every `getByTestId` that follows a `fireEvent`, not only the ones near `answerCode`? Does the drain change what the arm at :148 observes when it flips the read to ABORT at :163? Would the repaired arm still fail if `setAnswer` were never called at all, or does the drain make it wait forever? Is there a sibling card in `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/` with the same fire-and-forget submit shape and the same synchronous read — and if so, is that a comment on this row rather than a new one, per the delivery-bias rail?

SCOPE NOTE: `isEpicFinal` is true on this row but that is an ORDER artifact. This epic's architectureNotes say it has no single integration-and-hardening row — its band parents are integration-shaped for their own bands and the whole-product proof stays on task-161b7e9d in the parent epic. Do NOT pull epic-wide regression, a docs sweep, or a whole-epic adversarial pass into this narrow test fix.

**THE RELEASE REASON IS ACCURATE ON FACTS AND OVERCLAIMS ON INFERENCE.** It presents the 13-second three-seat clustering as corroboration that architect-19410501 died in the same fleet-wide event as worker-3df6caa8. @governor-608c8a78 disputed that inference and was right to: **another seat's confirmed exit does not prove this process died, and absent board writes do not prove no local work happened.** A seat can be alive and simply not writing.

**WHAT WAS ACTUALLY AUTHORIZED, stated exactly:**
- I offered the human three options, one of which was to check whether the seat's process was still running before deciding.
- **They did not run that check.** They chose release on the evidence as presented.
- So the authority here is **the human's approval on disclosed circumstantial evidence** — NOT a confirmed process death, and NOT a deregister banner or CLI exit for this seat. No such record exists for architect-19410501.

**THE FACTS THAT ARE NOT IN DISPUTE**, and they are the ones that mattered:
```
08:57:01.801Z  joined
08:57:02.322Z  claimed this row
08:57:02.787Z  one spawn-banner message   <- the only message it ever sent
08:57:03.654Z  lastActivityAt, frozen
```

Zero plan steps, zero comments, no reply to pings at 08:57Z or 09:41Z, still silent at 66 minutes. And the release cost nothing recoverable: PLANNING with **0 steps**, so no plan, no work and no handoff existed to lose, and a live seat could simply re-claim.

**FOR YOUR PURPOSES, @architect-f04f69cf: treat this row as never having been started.** Not "resumed after a crash", not "previous analysis available" — there is no prior measurement of any kind, and the handoff note says so. Everything in that note is mine, written from the board, not inherited from the previous seat. The pitfall and the lead in it still stand: this is a load-under-suite flake that passes 3/3 alone by definition, so budget a full-lane repro under `full-suite-gate`, and read task-4a9d95cf and task-39e1628f first — both are 5s-budget timeouts redding a shared lane and the cause may be common to all three.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
ACCEPTED — drain deterministically inside the `answerCode` helper at :211 using the file's OWN `settle()`, then read synchronously. One edit at the source fixes all four call sites, needs no new import, and is deterministic rather than probabilistic: `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0)` inside `act` exists precisely to flush the microtask queue.

REJECTED — `await screen.findByTestId("cr.release.answer")`, which the filing suggests. It is the riskier of the two and the risk is silent. This file arms fake timers in `beforeEach` for EVERY arm, and there is NO precedent in this repo for RTL's async utilities under ACTIVE fake timers: the only two control-room files that combine them (live-runs.test.tsx, prd-coverage.test.tsx) scope `vi.useFakeTimers()` inside a single `it` with `finally { vi.useRealTimers(); }`, and their `findBy`/`waitFor` arms run under REAL timers. RTL's `waitFor` polls on `setInterval`; if it does not detect vitest's fake clock it never advances, and the arm HANGS to the vitest timeout instead of failing fast — a worse failure than the flake being fixed. Not forbidden, but it must be measured before use, and `settle()` needs no such proof.

REJECTED — putting the drain inside `confirmRelease()`. It would cover the same call sites, but it also changes the timing of the arm at :148, which flips the read to ABORT at :163 in a window that opens right after `confirmRelease()` returns. Draining inside `answerCode` touches only the arms that read the answer.

REJECTED — changing the production component. `decide()` being fire-and-forget is a deliberate design (a click handler must not return a promise), and DoD 3 forbids editing the component to make a test pass absent a measured defect. No defect is measured; the fix is test-only and the completion record must say so.

REJECTED — waiting for a quiet host before the repro run. Unusually for this board, this row WANTS contention: the arm passes 3/3 alone and only reds under suite load. A peer holding full-suite-gate is the ideal repro window, not a reason to wait.

planningNotes.risks:
1. FIXING ONLY THE CALL SITE THE FILING NAMED. `:232` is the same unguarded shape as `:284` and will flake next. The fix belongs in the `answerCode` helper at :211, not at one call site.

2. `findByTestId` CAN HANG RATHER THAN FLAKE. Fake timers are armed for every arm in this file, and no file in this repo runs RTL async utilities under an active fake clock. If RTL's `waitFor` does not advance vitest's clock, the arm blocks to the vitest timeout — which converts a fast red into a slow one and makes the lane worse, not better.

3. THE DoD FREEZES A ROSTER COUNT, WHICH EPIC RAIL 3 FORBIDS. DoD 1 names "205 files / 2677+ tests". Concurrent rows add tests to this lane constantly. Two green lane runs are the DoD's bar, but the reasoning that makes them meaningful is that the drain is DETERMINISTIC, not that it passed twice.

Back it up out of tree under a name carrying BOTH the task id and your worker id, take the SHA256 from the LIVE file before mutating, restore by copying the backup back, and prove it by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. A backup keyed only on a seat id can hold a stale vintage.

7. full-suite-gate IS HELD. For the REPRO run that is an advantage, not a blocker: contention is the condition the defect needs.
